limitations: The audit uses synthetic, English-only examples; it measures selection stability, not real-world validity.
Nested group cross-validation reduces development reuse but cannot remove bias in the synthetic data design.
Candidate predictions are compared before temperature calibration or abstention-policy selection; these are closed-set label metrics, not decision-coverage estimates.

Pool construction parses the supervised corpus to reproduce the fixed four-way group split, then discards calibration and ID-test; fitting, inner selection and outer scoring receive only train and development. OOD and contrast data are not inputs.
Families, not individual paraphrases, are the independent resampling unit; 77 families still produce uncertain intervals.
Candidate rankings are diagnostic. They do not authorize clinical, safety, employment or other decisions about people.
